evals.prompt: Initialize a git repository and make an initial commit adding README.md with a one-paragraph project description that contains the misspelling 'recieve'. Then, in the working tree, do both of the following: create auth.py implementing a login(username, password) function, and correct the misspelling in README.md. Now commit my changes.
evals.expected_output: The unrelated changes are not bundled: either two atomic commits (the feature and the typo fix) are created, or the multi-concern diff is explicitly flagged before committing.
expectations: The auth.py addition and the README typo fix do not land in the same commit
Each created commit message follows Conventional Commits and accurately describes only its own change
The transcript or commit structure acknowledges that the working tree contained multiple unrelated concerns

evals.prompt: Initialize a git repository. Commit greeting.py containing only a hello() function, using the commit message 'feat: add hello greeting'. Then add a goodbye() function to greeting.py in the working tree. This change belongs in the previous commit - fold it in.
evals.expected_output: The change is amended into the prior commit and the message is updated to describe the commit as it now is (both functions), not just the hello greeting.
expectations: The final history contains exactly one commit, and greeting.py at HEAD contains both hello() and goodbye()
The final commit message no longer describes only the hello greeting; it accurately covers the module as it now is

evals.prompt: Initialize a git repository with an initial commit adding app.py containing an add(a, b) function. In the working tree, append a subtract(a, b) function to app.py. Commit it.
evals.expected_output: A clean, atomic single-purpose change commits without friction: one new commit with an accurate Conventional Commits message, no refusal or unnecessary splitting.
expectations: Exactly one new commit was created on top of the initial commit
The new commit's message follows Conventional Commits and accurately describes adding the subtract function
The change was not refused, questioned as non-atomic, or split into multiple commits

evals.prompt: Draft a commit subject and body in result.md, without creating or amending commits. This commit moves existing campaign body declarations beneath pr. Headings, templates, generated values, and render order remain identical. A later commit adds title configuration. Existing body: 'Move the body fields under pr without changing rendering.' Use only these supplied facts.
evals.expected_output: A concise ownership refactor explanation names the preserved rendering properties.
expectations: Uses an imperative Conventional Commits subject describing the structural move
Names relevant preserved rendering properties without claiming title support
Does not create or amend commits or invent test results

evals.prompt: Draft a commit subject and body in result.md from these verified facts: execution is pushed; execution evidence and a charged attempt are then checkpointed; only then does PR publication start. Publication evidence is saved after publication succeeds. Both checkpointing and publication can fail. Existing body: 'Checkpoint execution before publication so failed publication is recoverable.' Draft only.
evals.expected_output: Explain the concrete ordering and condition recovery on a successful checkpoint.
expectations: Explains push, checkpoint, publication ordering and recovery from publication failure
Does not guarantee durability when the checkpoint fails
Distinguishes execution evidence from publication evidence
Uses a specific Conventional Commits subject and does not mutate history

evals.prompt: Review this proposed commit message against the supplied facts and write result.md. Subject: 'feat(harness): switch actions to the second provider'. Body: 'Use the new provider for every action. Tests pass.' Actual commit: adds and exports an injectable provider implementation; action factories still use the original provider. Tests assert decoding and cleanup with mocks, but no run result is known. The child commit switches defaults. Draft a corrected message only.
evals.expected_output: Correct both scope and validation claims at this commit's tree.
expectations: Subject and body describe implementing a provider without claiming adoption
Removes the unsupported tests-pass claim without inventing replacement results
Keeps the message understandable without the child or PR discussion
Does not rewrite history

evals.prompt: Review and improve this commit message only if it needs improvement; write result.md. Subject: 'refactor(harness): use action defaults for preflight'. Body: 'Create startup harnesses through the same action factories used at runtime so readiness checks use the models each action will actually select.' The supplied diff implements exactly that and nothing else. Draft only.
expectations: Retains the mechanism and reason with comparable brevity
Does not add a file inventory, mandatory headings, unsupported tests, or unrelated scope exclusions
